description: Add a data seeding step to the deploy-pr.yml workflow that copies all data from the production DynamoDB table into the PR preview stack's DynamoDB table after deployment
steps: In .github/workflows/deploy-pr.yml, after the 'CDK Deploy PR stack' step, add a new step called 'Seed PR database from production'. This step should: (1) Read the production table name from the main stack's CloudFormation resources using `aws cloudformation describe-stack-resources` filtering for the DynamoDB table (resource type AWS::DynamoDB::Table), or alternatively use `aws cloudformation list-stack-resources` to find the table. (2) Read the PR stack's table name the same way. (3) Use `aws dynamodb scan` to read all items from the production table (handling pagination with --starting-token if LastEvaluatedKey is returned). (4) Use `aws dynamodb batch-write-item` to write the items into the PR table in batches of up to 25 items (DynamoDB BatchWriteItem limit). (5) Handle the case where the production table might be empty gracefully (just skip with a message). (6) Log how many items were copied.

The script should be written as inline bash in the workflow step. Use a while loop for pagination of the scan. Use jq to transform scan output into batch-write-item format. The batch-write-item payload needs the table name and PutRequest items.

Add a CfnOutput for the DynamoDB table name in apps/infra/src/stacks/recipe-manager-stack.ts so it can be easily retrieved from CloudFormation outputs. Add it as 'TableName' output with the value recipesTable.tableName. This makes retrieval simpler and more reliable than querying stack resources.

Ensure the seeding step is idempotent - if run multiple times (e.g., on synchronize events), it should overwrite existing data cleanly. Since PutRequest in batch-write overwrites existing items with the same key, this is naturally idempotent.
acceptance_criteria: The deploy-pr.yml workflow has a new step after CDK deploy that reads data from the prod table and writes it to the PR table
The script handles pagination correctly (production table could have more than 1MB of data)
The script handles empty production tables gracefully
The script uses batch-write-item with maximum 25 items per batch
A new CfnOutput named 'TableName' exists in the CDK stack
The infra app still builds successfully with `pnpm nx build infra`
The workflow YAML is syntactically valid
